rationales.privilege-grant: GRANT of a named privilege on a named object to a named role list. Approval is on this exact statement: the grantee list can never contain PUBLIC (Tier 0 refuses it), and the privilege must be the minimum the served function or path requires. Changing the object, the privilege or the grantee list changes the statement identity and forces re-approval.
rationales.privilege-grant-all-service-role: GRANT ALL on public.workspaces and public.workspace_memberships to service_role only. service_role holds BYPASSRLS by platform design, is never reachable from the browser and is the single server-side role used by the evidence service; the grant is scoped to those two tables and excludes every API role.
rationales.privilege-revoke: REVOKE from API roles. Revocation only narrows the privilege surface; the surrounding file re-grants the minimum set that remains, and re-running the migration is idempotent.
rationales.temporary-schema-ddl-window: Temporary CREATE on schema public granted to snapshot_publisher_owner so the same migration can create the objects that role owns, then revoked later in the same file. The window is closed inside the file and the final schema ACL is asserted by the pgTAP ACL probes.
rationales.rls-policy-create: CREATE POLICY on a workspace or snapshot relation. Permissive-versus-restrictive, the covered command and the targeted roles are pinned by the pgTAP policy-signature assertions (supabase/tests/source_snapshots.test.sql and source_snapshot_storage.test.sql), so a silent widening of this policy fails the test suite as well as this guard.
rationales.rls-policy-alter: ALTER POLICY rewrites the USING / WITH CHECK expression of an existing policy. The command/kind/role signature that results is pinned by the same pgTAP assertions; the expression itself is reviewed against the workspace-membership predicate it is meant to enforce.
rationales.rls-policy-drop: DROP POLICY IF EXISTS removes a superseded policy that the same file replaces. Dropping on its own never widens access: RLS stays default-deny and the intended policy is recreated in the same migration.
rationales.relation-alter: ALTER TABLE on an existing relation: constraint, trigger wiring, column or RLS flag. Enabling or forcing RLS narrows access; disabling it would be Tier 0 and cannot reach the ledger. The resulting catalogue state is asserted by the migration guard tests.
rationales.function-definition: Defines or replaces a function body. Any SECURITY DEFINER body must declare SET search_path or Tier 0 refuses it. Behaviour is covered by the Python service tests and, for the verifier, by the identity pgTAP suite which re-asserts the ACL and the role invariants.
rationales.function-ownership: ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO moves the function to snapshot_publisher_owner so the read fences evaluate against a stable owner. The ownership graph is asserted by the identity suite, which also pins the role invariants (NOLOGIN, NOINHERIT, NOBYPASSRLS).
rationales.procedural-block: DO block, i.e. server-side procedural SQL. Its body is a single opaque unit for the statement lexer, which is precisely why DO is registry-gated: it is the only construct that can wrap arbitrary statements behind an innocuous verb. Each block is approved as a whole, so adding one is always a visible ledger change.
rationales.catalog-seed-write: INSERT ... SELECT into a reviewed catalogue table (the read-policy baseline). Values come from pg_catalog and pg_policies, not from user input; the row set is what the inventory guard diffs against later.
rationales.temp-relation-cleanup: DROP TABLE on a pg_temp relation created earlier in the same file by the admin-audit guard. Scoped to the migration session; nothing outside pg_temp is touched.
rationales.catalog-assertion-call: Calls a private.* assertion or seeding function (assert_snapshot_role_safe, assert_snapshot_verifier_function_acl_safe, assert_snapshot_verifier_allowlist_shape, ensure_snapshot_bucket). These are fail-closed self-checks and idempotent catalogue seeds defined by reviewed migrations; they take literal arguments, never user input.
rationales.lifecycle-function-ownership: Transfers the Auth lifecycle provisioning trigger function to the dedicated NOLOGIN, NOINHERIT, NOBYPASSRLS provisioning role. The role is not granted to API/Auth identities; the migration's final privilege audit verifies those role attributes and memberships.
rationales.fail-closed-rls-bootstrap: DO block that replaces public.rls_auto_enable() with the reviewed fail-closed body. It refuses to replace a body that is neither the reviewed fail-open nor the reviewed fail-closed definition, re-raises ALTER failures with the table identity and the original SQLSTATE, asserts pg_class.relrowsecurity afterwards, and re-verifies the signature, owner, SECURITY DEFINER flag, fixed search_path, ACL and the ensure_rls event trigger. supabase/tests/rls_auto_enable.test.sql (plan 18) pins the observable contract and stops a silent revert to log-and-continue.
rationales.lifecycle-view-definition: Defines the private account-lifecycle self projection. It exposes only subject_id, state, and row_version through a security-invoker view; the surrounding migration grants it only to authenticated and keeps request_id and transition metadata private.
rationales.lifecycle-table-definition: Defines the authoritative account lifecycle relation with constrained states, trusted transition metadata, request references, and a monotonic row version. RLS, forced RLS, grants, policies, and privilege assertions in the same migration bound access.
rationales.lifecycle-comment: Documents the lifecycle relation and server-managed fields so the fail-closed state contract and retention boundary remain explicit without changing runtime privileges.
rationales.personal-api-key-function-ownership: Transfers the personal API key management and read RPCs to dedicated NOLOGIN, NOINHERIT, NOBYPASSRLS roles created in the same file. The temporary SET grants used only for ownership transfer are revoked before commit; the reader RPCs additionally require a one-use HMAC gateway proof and remain subject to forced RLS.
rationales.personal-api-key-schema-ddl-window: Temporary CREATE on schema public/private granted to the personal API key manager and reader so the same migration can transfer function ownership. The window is revoked in the same file; those roles never create tables or policies at runtime.
rationales.connector-workspace-backfill: Backfill existing connector connections to a personal workspace selected from active owner memberships; no user input and no cross-tenant access.
rationales.task-ledger-service-role-grant: GRANT ALL on the content-free public.task_run_ledger to service_role. service_role is server-only, never browser-reachable, and this grant is limited to the ledger relation; authenticated retains only SELECT and INSERT through membership-scoped RLS.
